# Paramaṭṭhaka Sutta (Snp 4.5 (PTS Snp 156))

**ID:** Snp 4.5 (PTS Snp 156)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Paramaṭṭhaka Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paramaṭṭhaka Sutta* is the fifth discourse of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* in the *Suttanipāta*, comprising eight verses (Sn 796–803; PTS Snp 156) [Anderson & Smith 1913; Hayes 1988; Hazra 1994; Saddhatissa 2013]. Its central theme is the critique of dogmatism and intellectual conceit: treating one's own views (*diṭṭhi*) or practices as "supreme" or ultimate (*parama*) causes one to look down on others as inferior, inevitably entangling the practitioner in verbal dispute, mental agitation, and attachment [Hayes 1988; McMahan 2002; Saddhatissa 2013]. The text emphasizes that the unattached sage relinquishes all grasping after opinions, notions of self, and dependence upon knowledge or conventional apperceptions (*saññā*), forming neither bias nor dogmatic construction (*pakappitā natthi aṇū pi saññā*) based on what is seen, heard, or thought [Pande 1974; Ruegg & Schmithausen 1990; Sciberras 2011].

 DharmaNexus computes 34 text-reuse matches with Mnd 5 across 3,397 shared characters, confirming the thorough integration of the verses into the canonical commentary, and registers automated cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Bodhisattvapiṭaka* (*ārya-bodhisattvapiṭaka-nāma-mahāyānasūtra*, D0056) [DharmaNexus].
